newsitem.title: USA: Ford not through restructuring European units.
newsitem.headline: Ford not through restructuring European units.

text.p: Ford Motor Co, which reported record quarterly profits for the second period Wednesday, said it is on track to improve its European results for all of 1997, but Ford Chairman Alex Trotman cautioned the company is not through restructuring its European operations to lower costs and improve efficiencies.
"We know more actions will be needed to achieve our long- term objectives," he said in a statement.
Ford posted second quarter earnings of $2.53 billion, or $2.06 a share, versus $1.90 billion, or $1.56 a share a year ago.
The second quarter earnings were an all-time quarterly record for the U.S. No. 2 automaker.
Included in the results were European profits of $157 million, a decline from $196 million. In South America, Ford reported a profit of $25 million versus a loss of $69 million.

"A strong automotive industry in Brazil and Argentina, growing customer demand for Ford products and cost efficiencies all are contributing to the improvement," Trotman said. "As we rebuild our business in the region, our focus on the fundamentals is resulting in faster progress than we first throught," he said.
